key_insight: BrickBench introduces a new way to test whether AI agents can design LEGO-style structures that are both semantically correct and physically buildable. It evaluates not just if the output matches the prompt, but whether the design can actually be assembled from available parts.
problem_solved: Current text-to-design systems often optimize for visual or semantic similarity without ensuring the design is physically realizable. This paper addresses the challenge of agentic design under discrete part constraints, where an agent must balance local assembly rules, global structure, and prompt alignment.
method: Introduces BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design.
Scores agents across validity, alignment, and design quality in three settings with different scales and part inventories.
Provides BrickAgent, an environment for coding and testing assembly plans against physical and semantic constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, BrickBench offers a realistic evaluation target for embodied and generative agents that must reason over discrete actions and constraints. It can help identify models that are truly useful for design tasks, not just good at producing plausible-looking outputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt -> agent -> part selection -> assembly validation

paper_authors: Peter Kulits, Yiqing Xu, R. Kenny Jones, Cordelia Schmid, Jiajun Wu
